issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch in Bitmap24: the template header declares Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) while the implementation (Bitmap24.cpp) defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height). This mismatch causes an out-of-class definition that does not match any declaration and will prevent the example_program from compiling. The solution repository uses the two-parameter constructor (int i_width, int i_height), which confirms the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template header to declare the two-parameter constructor matching the implementation and solution: change Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth); to Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height); (or alternatively adjust the implementation to provide the three-parameter constructor). Prefer updating the header to the two-parameter signature to match the implementation and the solution.

issues.description: Constructor signature for the Bitmap24 class is inconsistent between the template header and the implementation/solution. The template header declares Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) while the implementation (Bitmap24.cpp) defines a two-argument constructor Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height) and the solution header also declares a two-argument constructor. This mismatch creates confusion for students about the intended constructor API and may lead to compile errors or wasted time searching for the 'depth' parameter usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template header to match the intended two-argument constructor signature: declare Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height); (remove the 'depth' parameter), so header, implementation, and solution are consistent.
